verdict.confidence: High confidence on the balance sheet, low visibility on the outcome
verdict.summary: Innventure is an Orlando holding company that licenses technology out of multinationals and funds the ventures built to commercialise it. Nasdaq classifies it under Financial Services, industry Asset Management, and it employs 169 people. Plenty of readers will mistake it for an operating technology company. It is not one. The share price is not the interesting number here. The cash is: $55,367,000 on hand at 31 March 2026 against $34,031,000 of operating cash consumed in that single quarter, with a shelf registration effective since 8 April that carries a $75.0M standby equity purchase agreement. Second-quarter results land on 13 August.
whyBuy: Accelsius, the data-centre cooling venture, published independent benchmarks on 21 July 2026 showing two-phase direct-to-chip cooling delivering 9°C lower NVIDIA B200 junction temperatures than single-phase in warm-water conditions. Liquid cooling is the one capex line nobody in the sector is trimming.

Refinity secured an exclusive licence to PNNL catalyst technology on 22 June 2026, then appointed Zeton on 23 July to design and build a modular plastics-to-olefins plant intended as a repeatable commercial template. Those are engineering commitments, not slideware.
At $3.42 the stock changes hands at 1.23x its $2.79 stated book value. If the carrying value of the venture stakes survives audit, the arithmetic distance down to book is 18%, not 60%.

The January placement cleared at $3.50 with a funded institutional book behind it. The last close sits 2.3% below where those buyers were filled, which is a narrow discount for a name down 56.5% from its high.
8,793,478 shares are short, 12.9% of the float, at 6.8 days to cover on the latest official settlement. Funding news that removes the solvency question forces that position to cover into a thin book.
whyAvoid: Operating cash burn of $34,031,000 in Q1 2026 against $55,367,000 of cash at 31 March. On that run rate the balance covers 1.6 quarters from the end of March, which expires around now.

The funding channel is already built and effective: a shelf effective 8 April 2026 registering 41,291,719 resale shares and disclosing a standby equity purchase agreement with Yorkville for up to $75.0M, drawable at the company's discretion. That facility alone equals 26% of the market capitalisation.
Shares outstanding went from 49,547,673 in November 2024 to 84,044,748 in May 2026, a 69.6% increase. The November 2025 to March 2026 leg alone added 17,597,348 shares, up 28.2% in four months.
Insiders sold $19,776,678 of stock over the past twelve months against $244,245 bought, a ratio of 81 to 1. The last open-market purchase by anyone was 2 December 2025.
Enterprise value of $526,751,456 against $3,275,000 of revenue is 160.8x sales, on a company whose operating margin is -1,891.7%.

business.overview:
Innventure, Inc. (NasdaqGM: INV) was founded in 2015 and is headquartered in Orlando, Florida. Its stated model is to identify, fund and operate companies built around sustainable technology acquired or licensed from multinational corporations. In practice it is a holding company: it takes technology that a large corporate has shelved, wraps a venture around it, funds that venture, and consolidates the result.

That structure matters more than any product story, because it dictates how the accounts behave. Revenue at the parent is $3,275,000. The reported quarterly earnings swing violently in both directions, and not because the operating business is volatile. A holding company books revaluations of its stakes, and those revaluations dwarf the trading. Nasdaq classifies the company under Financial Services, industry Asset Management, with 169 full-time employees. Anyone underwriting this as a cooling-technology company or a recycling company is underwriting the wrong entity.

The ventures themselves are real and are moving. Accelsius sells two-phase direct-to-chip cooling into data centres. Refinity is building plastics-to-olefins capacity and has licensed catalyst technology from Pacific Northwest National Laboratory. Both produced verifiable third-party milestones in June and July 2026. Neither yet produces the cash the parent consumes.

technicals.setupNote: The three moving averages sit in descending order above the price: EMA20 at 3.7659, EMA50 at 4.5256, EMA200 at 4.8381. That is a downtrend with the structure intact, not a stock consolidating after a shock. The last close of $3.42 sits 9.2% under the 20-day and 29.3% under the 200-day. RSI at 41.9 is not oversold, which removes the usual bounce argument. MACD at -0.4999 has crossed marginally above its signal line at -0.5769, the only constructive reading on the board, and a single cross of that size after a 56% decline is noise until price confirms it. ATR of $0.4286 is 12.5% of the share price, so a normal session moves this stock more than a bad quarter moves most large caps. Position sizing has to start from that number. Verified support sits at 2.80, then 2.52, then the 52-week low at 2.36. Verified resistance does not begin until 5.21, which is 52% above the last close. There is nothing structural between $3.42 and $2.80 to lean on.

macro.impact: The tape is not the problem. A risk-on regime is exactly the environment in which a micro-cap with a funding need gets funded rather than left to fail, which is precisely why the equity facility is the base case rather than insolvency. Read the regime as raising the odds of dilution, not of collapse.

risks.riskSummary: One risk dominates and it is arithmetic. $55,367,000 of cash at 31 March against $34,031,000 consumed in the quarter just ended gives 1.6 quarters of cover from that date. Four months and change have since passed. The company has an effective shelf and a $75.0M equity facility sitting ready, which is the reason to expect a raise rather than a failure. Dilution here is not a risk to be weighed against others. It is a schedule.

riskCards.title: Cash runway measured in weeks, not years
points: Cash and equivalents of $55,367,000 at 31 March 2026, per the Q1 results release.
Net cash used in operating activities of $34,031,000 in Q1 2026 alone, per the company's own XBRL filing.
That is 39.7% above the Q4 2025 rate and 68.7% above the FY2025 quarterly average of $20.2M. Burn is accelerating, not stabilising.
$55.367M divided by $34.031M gives 1.63 quarters of cover from 31 March, which lands around late August 2026.
An EBITDA-based calculation gives a gentler seven months. I use the statement of cash flows instead, because it is what actually left the bank.
riskCards.verdict: The 13 August release will show the answer rather than the estimate. Until then this is the only number that governs the equity.

riskCards.title: The equity facility is already loaded
points: Shelf registration filed 18 March 2026 and declared effective 8 April 2026.
It registers up to 41,291,719 shares for resale by selling stockholders, which is 60.5% of the current 68,293,081 float.
YA II PN, Ltd. (Yorkville) alone accounts for 16,309,741 of those shares, 23.9% of the float.

The same document discloses a standby equity purchase agreement of up to $75.0M of common stock with drawdowns at the company's discretion. At $3.42 that is roughly 21.9 million new shares, a further 26% on the count.

The shelf also covers Series B and Series C preferred stock, convertible debentures and four separate warrant classes (Innventure, 2024 WTI, 2025 WTI and Series A). Individual strikes and expiries are not restated here because I did not verify them line by line.
riskCards.verdict: The company does not need to negotiate a financing. It needs to press a button. Price that.

riskCards.title: Insider selling is one-directional
points: Twenty-five open-market sales against five purchases in the twelve months to 30 June 2026.
WE-INN LLC sold 3,100,513 shares across fourteen filings between October and December 2025 for roughly $11.92M.
Director Daniel J. Hennessy sold 1,023,980 shares for roughly $5.53M, including 582,139 shares at $5.52 on 20 April 2026. He resigned from the board nine days later, on 29 April.
Chief Strategy Officer John Stewart Scott sold 452,668 shares at $5.13 on 26 November 2025 for $2,322,187.
Against that, five purchases totalling 58,786 shares and $244,245, all of them between 20 November and 2 December 2025. Nothing since.
Awards, gifts and tax-withholding dispositions are excluded from both counts. Only codes P and S are counted.
riskCards.verdict: $19,776,678 sold against $244,245 bought, 81 dollars out for every dollar in, and the buying stopped eight months ago at prices around $5.

riskCards.title: Valuation has no anchor except book
points: Enterprise value of $526,751,456 on $3,275,000 of revenue is 160.8x sales.
Operating margin of -1,891.7% and return on equity of -47.4%.
Forward P/E of -57.0x confirms the loss and prices nothing.

The mean analyst target of $14.50 is four times the last close, but the coverage record shows zero upgrades, zero downgrades and zero initiations, with neutral sentiment. Nobody has revisited that number. Do not use it.
The one defensible anchor is stated book value of $2.79 per share, 18% below the last close.
riskCards.verdict: Book is the floor that can be argued from data. Everything above it rests on venture stakes the market cannot independently mark.

riskCards.title: Governance turnover around the funding cliff
points: Two Item 3.01 listing-rule notices filed in 2026, both concerning Nasdaq Listing Rule 5605(c)(2)(A) on audit committee composition after Daniel Hennessy's resignation left the committee with two members.
Cured: Bruce Brown was appointed on 15 May 2026 and Nasdaq confirmed restored compliance on 19 May 2026. This was never a price or market-value deficiency.
Chief executive succession announced 30 June 2026: Dr. Bill Grieco replaces Bill Haskell, who retired.
The vendor compliance flag reads false today, which is correct, and would have concealed the whole episode had the filings not been read.
riskCards.verdict: Resolved on the substance. Worth stating plainly rather than leaving as an unexplained red flag in a filings list.

riskCards.title: Where the data disagrees with itself
points: The quoted price of $3.42 is the close of 5 August 2026, not a live price. The quote arrived roughly 19 hours old while its own session block described the 6 August session as open, and no 6 August bar existed at the time of writing. Every level in this note is anchored to the 5 August close.
Cost to borrow could not be retrieved at all. The feed returned a decoding error on this symbol. There is no borrow-cost figure in this analysis, and an absent value is not a low one.

Support and resistance came back empty from one endpoint at 15:06 UTC and complete from another at 15:09 UTC, same symbol, same day. The levels used here (2.80 / 2.52 / 2.36 and 5.21 / 5.57 / 5.96) are the ones from the second call.

Short interest as a share of float reads 12.05% from one source and 12.876% from the official FINRA series, on the identical 8,793,478 shares. The gap is the float denominator: roughly 72.97M implied versus the stated 68,293,081. I use the FINRA figure.
Days to cover reads 5.28, 6.19 and 6.83 depending on which source is asked. I use 6.83, the official 15 July settlement.

Enterprise value of $526,751,456 does not reconcile to market cap plus debt minus cash, which gives $258,771,056. The $268.0M gap is unexplained by the data available, most plausibly non-controlling interests and preferred stock in a consolidated holding structure. The 160.8x sales multiple inherits that uncertainty.
Price-to-book of 1.2599 implies a $3.515 share price against book of $2.79. At the actual $3.42 close the ratio is 1.226x.
Forward P/E of -57.0 implies forward earnings near -$0.06 a share, which cannot be squared with the -$0.2967 reported for Q1 2026.

Runway itself depends on method: $55.4M against annualised EBITDA of -$94.8M gives about seven months, while the same cash against the $34.0M actually consumed in Q1 gives 4.9 months from 31 March. I lead with the cash-flow number because it is what left the bank rather than a derived margin.
riskCards.verdict: None of this changes the direction of the conclusion, and all of it changes how much precision the conclusion deserves. Where two sources disagreed I have said which one I used and why, rather than picking one quietly.

risks.pedagogy: A micro-cap with an open funding need does not trade on its products. It trades on the terms of its next financing. Every piece of good news from Accelsius or Refinity between now and that financing raises the price at which the company can issue, which is good for the company and neutral to negative for anyone who already owns the shares being diluted. That asymmetry is the whole position. Judge this name on the 13 August cash line first and the venture milestones second.

manipulations.hostileFundsVerdict: YA II PN, Ltd. (Yorkville) holds 16,309,741 registered resale shares, 23.9% of the float, and is the counterparty to the $75.0M standby equity purchase agreement. Standby facilities of this kind are drawn at a discount to prevailing market prices, which mechanically links each drawdown to downward pressure on the share price and to a larger share count on the next drawdown. That is the structure, stated neutrally; nothing here alleges misconduct by any party.
manipulations.integrityVerdict: No trading halt, no compliance flag, no failure-to-deliver threshold listing, and no most-shorted designation at the time of writing. The two 2026 listing-rule notices concerned audit committee composition and were cured on 19 May 2026. The pressure on this equity is structural and fully disclosed in the filings rather than anomalous.

tradeIdea.entryNote: Reference level, not a buy order. This map is bearish and it is drawn for managing an existing position, not for opening one.
tradeIdea.horizon: Through the 13 August print, roughly 5 to 20 sessions
tradeIdea.thesis: The downtrend is intact below the 20-day at 3.7659, and the first verified support is 18% lower at 2.80. A raise on the effective shelf is the base case rather than the tail case, and equity drawdowns at market price a stock toward its support, not its resistance. The invalidation is clean: a Q2 balance sheet that shows cash comfortably above $25M with the burn rate decelerating, or a reclaim of the 20-day that holds for three sessions, kills this map entirely.
catalysts: Q2 2026 results on 13 August 2026. Read cash and equivalents, then net cash used in operating activities, then the share count on the cover page, in that order.
Any drawdown notice on the $75.0M standby equity facility, or a new prospectus supplement off the effective shelf.
A named commercial contract at Accelsius. That is the one announcement that changes the funding terms rather than the funding need.
Resumption of insider buying. The last open-market purchase was 2 December 2025 at $5.06.
invalidation: Cash and equivalents above roughly $25M at 30 June with quarterly operating burn below $25M. That restores a year of visibility and the thesis is wrong.
A close above the 20-day at 3.7659 held for three consecutive sessions.
A financing struck at or above the last close instead of at a discount, which would signal demand rather than necessity.
Any insider open-market purchase of size.

globalScore.mindsetTip: Retail loses money on names like this by buying the product story and paying for it in share count. Set your position size from the ATR of 12.5% of price, decide in advance what the 13 August cash line has to say, and write that number down before the release rather than after it.
